exclusions.agent-tool-call-ids: a call object that is both streamed and in the final batch (the identity cases of the Node test) is not recorded: the Rust core receives the final batch as separate values; the same scenarios are recorded with separate values
exclusions.exec-deadline: holdEnd and holdEndAt come from Node's own armDeadlines (its text is taken from shell-command.mjs of the tree, which does not export it) run on timers and a clock the recorder owns and advances to each due timer; they are compared only for calls with background enabled and a hold above 0, the only ones whose wait reaches it;Node's timeout and promotedTimeoutMs are not compared (the core cuts the foreground window where it waits, from the same hold and cap); MIXDOG_SHELL_BACKGROUND_MAX_MS, an operator net the Node test does not cover, is not recorded: the core applies it to the foreground run as well as to the promoted job
exclusions.exec-env: the skill launcher directory is the recording's data folder under the sandbox: stored as <LAUNCHER>
exclusions.exec-hoist-long: the command text is not repeated in a plan that equals it (`<SAME>`, `<COMMAND>`): a 30 KB command would be stored three times; the replay compares the plan with the command it was given
exclusions.fs-list-page: NaN and Infinity are not recorded as head_limit: JSON carries neither (a client's request cannot hold them) and the recording would store null, a different input
exclusions.fs-markers: capMarker cursor/fullPath and windowMarker offsetKey are not recorded: the Rust markers have no caller that passes them
exclusions.scm-locks: the realpath spelling of the Node key test is textually the directory itself on the recording machine, so it is not a separate case; each key is recorded whole with the key of the sandbox root (a checkout-dependent prefix) replaced by <ROOT>, and the replay writes the core's `/` separators for the recorded `\`; the "rejected" outcome of an aborted wait is a list apart from the events, because the order of a promise's rejection handler against another task's start is a tick of Node's promise queue, not a behaviour

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder
